1.prologue: A king named Odysseus left his island of Ithaca to fight a ten-year war at Troy, and ten more years have passed without his return. At home his wife and son wait while a crowd of local men eat his food and press his wife to marry one of them and take his throne. Now the gods decide to bring him home.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the missing king trying to get home

cast.name: Telemachus
cast.who: Odysseus's son, about twenty

cast.name: Penelope
cast.who: Odysseus's wife, still waiting for him

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: the goddess who protects Odysseus and his son

cast.name: Zeus
cast.who: king of the gods, who decides

cast.name: Poseidon
cast.who: sea god, angry with Odysseus

cast.name: The suitors
cast.who: men who want Penelope and the throne

1.carry: Telemachus has decided to act: tomorrow he will face the suitors before the whole island, while far away his father is still trapped.

2.prologue: At dawn Telemachus calls the people of Ithaca together for the first time in twenty years and demands that the suitors leave his house. The suitors refuse and blame his mother. With Athena's help, he prepares to slip away by ship to find news of his father.

cast.name: Telemachus
cast.who: Odysseus's son, finding his courage

cast.name: Penelope
cast.who: his mother, who stalls the suitors

cast.name: Antinous
cast.who: the boldest and cruelest of the suitors

cast.name: Eurymachus
cast.who: a smooth-talking leader of the suitors

cast.name: Mentor
cast.who: old friend Odysseus left in charge

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: the goddess guiding Telemachus, often disguised

cast.name: Eurycleia
cast.who: the old nurse who raised father and son

2.carry: Telemachus is at sea without his mother's knowledge, and the suitors do not yet know he has gone.

3.prologue: Telemachus lands at Pylos, kingdom of an old king who fought beside his father at Troy. He hopes to learn what happened to Odysseus after the war. Athena travels with him, still disguised as his father's old friend Mentor.

cast.name: Telemachus
cast.who: Odysseus's son, searching for news

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: his protector goddess, disguised as Mentor

cast.name: Nestor
cast.who: old king of Pylos, fought at Troy

cast.name: Pisistratus
cast.who: Nestor's youngest son, Telemachus's companion

cast.name: Agamemnon
cast.who: leader of the war, murdered on returning

cast.name: Orestes
cast.who: Agamemnon's son, who avenged his father

3.carry: Nestor knew nothing certain, so Telemachus now heads to Sparta, to a king who came home last of all.

4.prologue: Telemachus reaches Sparta, ruled by Menelaus and his wife Helen, who both knew his father at Troy. They tell him stories of Odysseus and, at last, real news. Meanwhile, back on Ithaca, the suitors discover he has left.

cast.name: Telemachus
cast.who: Odysseus's son, searching for news

cast.name: Pisistratus
cast.who: Nestor's son, his traveling companion

cast.name: Menelaus
cast.who: king of Sparta, fought beside Odysseus

cast.name: Helen
cast.who: Menelaus's wife, whose capture started the war

cast.name: Proteus
cast.who: shape-changing sea god who knows the truth

cast.name: Antinous
cast.who: the boldest and cruelest of the suitors

cast.name: Penelope
cast.who: Telemachus's mother, waiting on Ithaca

4.carry: Odysseus is alive but trapped, and a band of suitors now lies in wait to murder his son on the way home.

5.prologue: Now we meet Odysseus himself, held for years on a remote island by Calypso, a goddess who loves him and wants him to stay. The gods order her to let him go. He must cross the sea alone, and the sea god Poseidon still hates him.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the missing king, seen at last

cast.name: Calypso
cast.who: a goddess who keeps him on her island

cast.name: Hermes
cast.who: messenger of the gods

cast.name: Zeus
cast.who: king of the gods, who orders his release

cast.name: Poseidon
cast.who: sea god, angry with Odysseus

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: the goddess who protects Odysseus

cast.name: Ino
cast.who: a sea goddess who saves him

5.carry: Odysseus lies naked and alone on a strange shore, his raft gone, among people who do not know who he is.

6.prologue: Odysseus has washed up on Scheria, island of a rich seafaring people called the Phaeacians. Athena arranges for the king's daughter to find him. Everything depends on whether a stranger with nothing will be helped.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the shipwrecked king, now a nameless stranger

cast.name: Nausicaa
cast.who: young princess of the island he reached

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: the goddess who protects Odysseus

cast.name: Alcinous
cast.who: Nausicaa's father, king of the Phaeacians

cast.name: Arete
cast.who: Nausicaa's mother, the queen

6.carry: Odysseus is about to enter the king's palace as a nameless beggar, hoping the queen will grant him a ship home.

7.prologue: Following the princess's advice, Odysseus walks into the Phaeacian city, hidden by a mist Athena wraps around him. He must win over the king and queen without revealing who he is. These people could carry him home by ship.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the shipwrecked king, still unnamed here

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: the goddess who protects Odysseus

cast.name: Alcinous
cast.who: king of the Phaeacians

cast.name: Arete
cast.who: the queen, whose favor he needs

cast.name: Nausicaa
cast.who: the princess who sent him here

7.carry: The Phaeacians have promised Odysseus a ship home, but they still do not know his name.

8.prologue: The Phaeacians hold a day of feasting, games, and songs for their unknown guest. A blind singer performs stories of the war at Troy, and some of them are about Odysseus himself. The guest's tears begin to give him away.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the guest who has not said his name

cast.name: Alcinous
cast.who: king of the Phaeacians, his host

cast.name: Demodocus
cast.who: the blind singer at the king's court

cast.name: Euryalus
cast.who: a young Phaeacian who insults Odysseus

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: the goddess who protects Odysseus

8.carry: Odysseus is about to reveal who he is and tell everything that happened to him after the war.

9.prologue: Odysseus names himself to the Phaeacians and begins to tell his story, so from here the film shows his memories of the years after the war. He left Troy with twelve ships full of men. This is how he started losing them, beginning with a giant's cave.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the king, now telling his own story

cast.name: The crew
cast.who: Odysseus's sailors from home

cast.name: Polyphemus
cast.who: one-eyed giant who traps them in his cave

cast.name: Poseidon
cast.who: sea god, Polyphemus's father

9.carry: By shouting his name, Odysseus has made the sea god Poseidon his enemy, which is why storms still pursue him.

10.prologue: Odysseus continues his story to the Phaeacians. Home comes within sight and is lost, most of his fleet is destroyed, and the survivors land on the island of a powerful enchantress. To go on, he must learn to bargain with her.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the king, still telling his story

cast.name: The crew
cast.who: Odysseus's sailors, fewer every year

cast.name: Aeolus
cast.who: keeper of the winds who helps them

cast.name: Eurylochus
cast.who: Odysseus's second-in-command, often doubting him

cast.name: Circe
cast.who: a goddess-witch who turns men into pigs

cast.name: Hermes
cast.who: messenger of the gods

cast.name: Elpenor
cast.who: a young sailor of the crew

10.carry: Odysseus is sailing to the edge of the world to speak with the dead, and one of his men lies unburied behind him.

11.prologue: Still telling his story, Odysseus describes his journey to the land of the dead. He goes to ask a dead prophet how to get home. There he also meets the ghosts of people he loved and soldiers he fought beside.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the king, still telling his story

cast.name: Elpenor
cast.who: the sailor who died on Circe's island

cast.name: Tiresias
cast.who: a blind prophet, now among the dead

cast.name: Anticleia
cast.who: Odysseus's mother, who died while he was away

cast.name: Agamemnon
cast.who: war leader, murdered by his wife at home

cast.name: Achilles
cast.who: the greatest Greek warrior, killed at Troy

11.carry: Odysseus now knows the warning: if his men harm the Sun god's cattle, he will lose them all.

12.prologue: Odysseus finishes his story with the last stage of the voyage. Circe warns him of the dangers ahead, and he faces them one by one. The worst danger turns out to be his own hungry crew.

cast.name: Odysseus
cast.who: the king, finishing his story

cast.name: The crew
cast.who: Odysseus's last surviving sailors

cast.name: Circe
cast.who: the goddess who now advises him

cast.name: Eurylochus
cast.who: his second-in-command, who stirs up the men

cast.name: The Sirens
cast.who: singers whose song lures sailors to death

cast.name: Scylla
cast.who: a six-headed monster on a cliff

cast.name: Zeus
cast.who: king of the gods, who punishes

12.carry: His story is told: this is how Odysseus came to be alone on Calypso's island, and now the Phaeacians must decide how to send him home.

OD-B01-S01.card: The gods meet, and Athena asks Zeus to let Odysseus go home, while the sea god who hates him is away.

OD-B01-S02.card: Athena plans to free Odysseus from the island where a goddess holds him, and to go herself to wake up his son.

OD-B01-S03.card: Disguised as a traveling stranger, Athena arrives at Odysseus's house, where the suitors are feasting, and Telemachus welcomes her in.

OD-B01-S04.card: Telemachus complains that the suitors are eating up his missing father's wealth; the disguised goddess tells him his father is alive.

OD-B01-S05.card: Athena tells Telemachus to stand up to the suitors in public and to sail away in search of news of his father.

OD-B01-S06.card: The goddess flies off like a bird; Telemachus, newly bold, sends his grieving mother upstairs and calls a public meeting for dawn.

OD-B02-S01.card: Telemachus summons the island to a meeting, sits in his father's seat, and stands to speak about the ruin of his house.

OD-B02-S02.card: Antinous blames Penelope, who stalled the suitors for years by weaving a burial cloth by day and secretly unpicking it at night.

OD-B02-S03.card: Two eagles fight above the crowd; an old seer says Odysseus is coming home to punish the suitors, and Eurymachus mocks him.

OD-B02-S04.card: Telemachus announces a voyage for news; Mentor scolds the people for doing nothing, but the suitors break up the meeting.

OD-B02-S05.card: Alone on the beach, Telemachus prays; Athena appears in Mentor's shape and promises to find him a ship and crew.

OD-B02-S06.card: Telemachus secretly orders supplies from the storeroom, and his old nurse Eurycleia, frightened, swears not to tell his mother.

OD-B02-S07.card: Athena gathers a crew, puts the suitors to sleep, and sails with Telemachus through the night.

OD-B03-S01.card: They arrive during a great sacrifice to the sea god; shy Telemachus is urged forward; Nestor's son welcomes them to the feast.

OD-B03-S02.card: Nestor asks who the strangers are; Telemachus names himself and begs for the plain truth about his father.

OD-B03-S03.card: Nestor remembers how the Greek fleet split after the war; Odysseus went another way, and Nestor never learned what became of him.

OD-B03-S04.card: Nestor tells how Agamemnon was murdered at home and his son Orestes avenged him, and urges Telemachus to be just as brave.

OD-B03-S05.card: The disguised companion suddenly flies off as a bird; Nestor realizes a goddess has been guiding Telemachus and prays to her.

OD-B03-S06.card: Nestor gives Telemachus horses and a chariot, and his son Pisistratus drives him overland toward Sparta.

OD-B04-S01.card: Telemachus and Pisistratus arrive at Sparta during a wedding feast, and King Menelaus welcomes them into his dazzling palace.

OD-B04-S02.card: When Menelaus speaks of Odysseus, Telemachus hides his tears; Helen recognizes him as Odysseus's son by his face, and all weep.

OD-B04-S03.card: Helen eases their grief with a drugged wine and recalls Odysseus sneaking into the enemy city disguised as a beggar.

OD-B04-S04.card: Menelaus recalls the hollow wooden horse that smuggled Greek soldiers into the enemy city, and how Odysseus kept the hidden men silent.

OD-B04-S05.card: Menelaus tells how he wrestled a shape-changing sea god, who revealed that Odysseus is alive but held captive on a goddess's island.

OD-B04-S06.card: Telemachus insists on leaving; the royal couple give him gifts, and Helen reads an eagle seizing a goose as Odysseus's coming revenge.

OD-B04-S07.card: On Ithaca, the suitors learn Telemachus has sailed and send a ship to ambush him; Penelope hears and collapses in fear.

OD-B05-S01.card: Zeus sends Hermes, the gods' messenger, flying over the sea to Calypso's island with the order to release Odysseus.

OD-B05-S02.card: Calypso protests that the gods resent goddesses who love mortal men, but she agrees to let Odysseus go.

OD-B05-S03.card: Odysseus suspects a trick until Calypso swears an oath; offered immortality with her, he still longs for his wife.

OD-B05-S04.card: With tools from Calypso, Odysseus builds a raft in four days, and she sends him off with food and a fair wind.

OD-B05-S05.card: Poseidon wrecks the raft with a storm; Ino, a sea goddess, gives Odysseus a veil and tells him to swim.

OD-B05-S06.card: After two days swimming, Odysseus finds a calm river mouth, crawls ashore on an unknown land, and sleeps under leaves.

OD-B06-S01.card: Athena appears in Princess Nausicaa's dream and urges her to wash clothes at the river, where Odysseus lies sleeping.

OD-B06-S02.card: Nausicaa and her maids wash clothes and play ball by the river; their shout wakes Odysseus.

OD-B06-S03.card: Naked and salt-caked, Odysseus covers himself with a branch and begs Nausicaa for help; her maids flee but she stands firm.

OD-B06-S04.card: Washed and dressed, Odysseus looks splendid; Nausicaa tells him to follow her to town and plead first with the queen.

OD-B07-S01.card: Disguised as a girl carrying water, Athena guides the hidden Odysseus through the city and tells him to seek out Queen Arete.

OD-B07-S02.card: Odysseus stands amazed before the king's palace, with its golden doors and an orchard that bears fruit all year.

OD-B07-S03.card: Odysseus kneels before Queen Arete and begs for passage home; after a long silence, the king raises him and promises a ship.

OD-B07-S04.card: The queen recognizes the clothes he wears; Odysseus tells of his shipwreck without giving his name, and King Alcinous promises him passage.

OD-B08-S01.card: Athena calls the people together and makes Odysseus look impressive; the king orders a ship and crew made ready for him.

OD-B08-S02.card: The blind singer Demodocus sings of the war at Troy, and Odysseus secretly weeps into his cloak; only the king notices.

OD-B08-S03.card: At the games a young man named Euryalus mocks the stranger, and Odysseus answers by throwing a discus farther than anyone.

OD-B08-S04.card: Demodocus sings of two gods caught in a net, dancers perform, and Euryalus apologizes with the gift of a sword.

OD-B08-S05.card: Odysseus asks for the song of the wooden horse, weeps again, and the king finally demands to know his name and story.

OD-B09-S01.card: At last Odysseus tells the court his name, says his home is Ithaca, and begins the story of his journey.

OD-B09-S02.card: Leaving Troy, his men raid a town and linger to feast against his orders, until the townspeople strike back and kill many.

OD-B09-S03.card: Some sailors eat the lotus, a plant that makes them forget home; Odysseus drags them weeping back to the ships.

OD-B09-S04.card: The fleet rests on an island near the land of the one-eyed giants, and Odysseus takes one ship to explore.

OD-B09-S05.card: Odysseus and twelve men find a cave full of food; the men want to steal and run, but he insists on waiting.

OD-B09-S06.card: The giant Polyphemus comes home, seals the cave with a huge stone, and discovers the strangers hiding inside.

OD-B09-S07.card: Odysseus asks for the kindness owed to guests, but Polyphemus scorns the gods and eats two of his men.

OD-B09-S08.card: Trapped, Odysseus sharpens a wooden stake in secret, then gives the giant strong wine and tells him his name is Nobody.

OD-B09-S09.card: They drive the burning stake into the giant's eye; when neighbors come, he shouts that Nobody is hurting him, so they leave.

OD-B09-S10.card: The men escape by clinging to the bellies of sheep as the blind giant lets his flock out to graze.

OD-B09-S11.card: Safe on the water, Odysseus boasts his real name; Polyphemus prays to his father Poseidon to make the homecoming late and lonely.

OD-B10-S01.card: Aeolus bottles the bad winds in a bag; within sight of home, the crew opens it and the winds blow them back.

OD-B10-S02.card: Cannibal giants hurl boulders into a harbor and destroy every ship but Odysseus's own, which was moored outside.

OD-B10-S03.card: On a new island the survivors rest, and Eurylochus leads half the men inland toward a house where smoke is rising.

OD-B10-S04.card: Circe welcomes the men with drugged food and turns them into pigs; only Eurylochus stays outside and runs back to warn Odysseus.

OD-B10-S05.card: Going alone to rescue them, Odysseus meets Hermes, who gives him a magic herb that will protect him from Circe's drug.

OD-B10-S06.card: Circe's spell fails on Odysseus; he draws his sword, and she swears an oath to do him no harm.

OD-B10-S07.card: Circe turns the pigs back into men; the whole crew stays with her for a year before they ask to go home.

OD-B10-S08.card: Circe says Odysseus must first consult a prophet in the land of the dead; Elpenor falls from a roof and dies unnoticed.

OD-B11-S01.card: At the edge of the world, Odysseus pours blood into a pit, and the ghosts of the dead swarm to drink.

OD-B11-S02.card: The first ghost is Elpenor, who begs Odysseus to go back and give his body a proper burial.

OD-B11-S03.card: The prophet Tiresias warns that the crew must not touch the Sun god's cattle, and that Odysseus will reach home alone.

OD-B11-S04.card: Odysseus meets his mother, who died of longing for him; three times he tries to hug her, and his arms pass through.

OD-B11-S05.card: A procession of famous women from old stories rises to drink the blood and tell who they were.

OD-B11-S06.card: Agamemnon's ghost tells how his wife and her lover murdered him on his homecoming, and warns Odysseus to return in secret.

OD-B11-S07.card: Achilles says death holds no glory, asks after his family, and strides off rejoicing to hear his son fought bravely.

OD-B11-S08.card: Odysseus sees the punished dead and famous heroes, until the crowding ghosts frighten him back to his ship.

OD-B12-S01.card: Back on Circe's island, the crew burns Elpenor's body and plants his oar on the grave, as promised.

OD-B12-S02.card: Circe privately describes each danger ahead and how to survive it, and warns Odysseus not to fight what cannot be fought.

OD-B12-S03.card: Odysseus plugs his men's ears with wax and has them tie him to the mast, so he can hear the Sirens safely.

OD-B12-S04.card: Avoiding a deadly whirlpool, they row close to the opposite cliff, where the monster Scylla snatches six men from the ship.

OD-B12-S05.card: On the island of the Sun god's cattle, the men swear not to touch them, but storms trap them for a month.

OD-B12-S06.card: While Odysseus sleeps, Eurylochus persuades the starving men to kill the sacred cattle; the Sun god demands revenge from Zeus.

OD-B12-S07.card: Zeus strikes the ship with lightning and every man drowns; Odysseus alone clings to the wreck and drifts to Calypso's island.
